key_insight: Evaporation of capillary bridges between curved surfaces is governed by a coupled thermo-fluid-adhesion process, where curvature and thermal conductivity strongly control mass transfer, Marangoni circulation, and adhesion loss.
engineering_relevance: The results inform the design of adhesive, thermal, and wetting-dependent microsystems by showing how surface curvature and material conductivity can tune capillary force and drying dynamics.
method: Computed equilibrium capillary bridge shapes with a level set method.
Simulated transient evaporation using an Arbitrary Lagrangian Eulerian (ALE) framework to track the moving liquid-vapor interface.
Performed parametric studies on substrate curvature, wettability, and solid thermal conductivity.
evidence_signal: The framework was validated against published results for capillary profiles, evaporation rates, and capillary forces, with good agreement.
watch_item: The findings depend on a fully coupled numerical model, so predictive accuracy may be sensitive to interface tracking, material-property assumptions, and boundary-condition specification.
paper_title: Interfacial-Thermo-Fluid-Adhesion Dynamics of Evaporating Capillary Bridges between Curved Surfaces
